data.claim: drift.measure can report code_behind (commits of HEAD..base with a path outside [worktree].behind_ignore_globs) beside the total, so an events-only advance gives behind 1, code_behind 0 and no merge commit.
data.falsifier: On the unfixed code a worktree whose base gained only an events commit reports behind 1 and sync/queue merge it: tests/test_code_behind.py must fail there and pass after the fix.
data.mechanism: measure already lists HEAD..base commits with their paths (--name-only), so the classification needs no second git query; sync, the queue and the hint all read measure, so one change reaches them.
data.probe: uv run pytest -n 8 tests/test_code_behind.py -q -x (before the fix, in the worktree)
data.probe_output: before fix: 8 failed (test_the_knob_defaults_to_the_event_log_directory, test_the_queue_skips_the_re_merge_when_main_moved_by_events_only, test_a_commit_touching_events_and_code_is_a_code_commit, test_the_ignore_list_is_the_users_to_widen, test_could_not_tell_stays_none, test_sync_check_says_current_when_main_moved_by_events_only, test_sync_reports_the_total_and_the_code_count_and_merges_when_code_moved, test_the_commit_gate_counts_only_code_commits_against_max_behind); after the fix: 18 passed in 9.37s

evidence.note: research Rdf5d988483 CONFIRMED: tests/test_code_behind.py failed 8 of 18 before the fix, 18 passed after

data.body:
Bug B1c1e1c9213 (ci/unit_tests baseline comparison uses current main so a worktree on an older base is judged baseline-red for failures it did not cause), D-premerge-precommit-gate-2026-11-12, rules r-feature-four-ways and r-company-workflows. Behaviour: [worktree] knobs (auto_sync default on, when: on claim and before a gate starts, strategy merge|rebase default merge, refuse_on_conflict) so an idle or waiting item's worktree is merged up to main once before its gates; conflicts are reported, never auto-resolved; never rewrites history on a branch with unmerged commits unless the strategy is rebase and the user chose it; never touches the primary checkout; four ways to configure (file, ddflow config, one MCP action on an existing family, prompt example). Tests: behind-main worktree is synced; conflict is reported not resolved; knob off leaves it; baseline comparison uses the item's base when merge is off. Related: fix-B1c1e1c9213, GM-known-red-registry.

Note from GM-code-behind: 'behind' is now code-behind. services/drift.measure returns code_behind (commits of HEAD..base touching a path outside [worktree].behind_ignore_globs, default .ddflow/) beside behind; the sync service, the queue re-merge, the commit gate and the session hint read it. Read DriftReport.code_behind (and rules) to decide whether to auto-sync: behind > 0 with code_behind == 0 and no rules is not a reason to merge.

evidence.note: commit 2b46e657a: knob worktree.behind_ignore_globs, DriftReport.code_behind, sync/queue/commit gate/session hint read it; tests/test_code_behind.py 18 passed; 68 related test files: 2867 passed, 16 failed all default.toml/pin staleness already red on main (pins regenerate --check on main lists the same 7 stale pins)

chunk_findings.detail: The test lands only `.ddflow/rules/r-x.md`, which is under the default ignore glob `.ddflow/`, so `code_behind` is `0` under the stated implementation. The ACCEPT rule says sync/queue should skip when code-behind is zero, and the other sync tests enforce that for events-only advances. This test nevertheless asserts `status == "merged"` and that the rule file is present in the worktree. Thus, with the specified default ignore list, the test should fail; if the implementation is changed to make it pass, the ignore knob no longer behaves as a simple path-ignore list and contradicts the intended “skip when K = 0” behavior.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_code_behind.py:test_sync_still_merges_when_a_rulebook_changed_in_the_ignored_directory

chunk_findings.detail: The fast path returns “current” only when `rep.rules` is empty. With the default `behind_ignore_globs=[".ddflow/"]`, a missing commit that changes only a rulebook under `.ddflow/` has `code_behind=0` but `rep.rules` non-empty, so branchsync falls through to status `behind` and, when `check=False`, proceeds to merge it. That creates the merge/sync signal the change is meant to remove for `K=0`; the rulebook case should remain drift (`stale_rules`) rather than making the tree “behind” for sync/queue re-merge.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/branchsync.py:260

chunk_findings.detail: The new threshold uses `(d.code or 0)` for the comparison but still interpolates `d.code` and `d.behind` directly in the message. The `Drift` dataclass explicitly allows `behind is None` (with `detail` explaining why), and TOML permits a negative integer for `max_behind`. Given `[enforce].max_behind = -1` and a drift result where the base could not be measured (`behind=None`, `code_behind=None`), the condition `(None or 0) > -1` is true, so the verdict is emitted as `... this branch is None commits behind ... None commits in all`. The same negative threshold also flags a branch with `code_behind=0` because `0 > -1`, contradicting the change’s rule that zero code-behind should not make `max_behind` act.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/enforce/driftchecks.py:181

chunk_findings.detail: The stated change defines “code behind” as `git rev-list --count HEAD..base -- . ':(exclude).ddflow'`, with `[worktree].behind_ignore_globs` defaulting to `[".ddflow/"]`. Under that definition, a main commit that only touches `.ddflow/rules/r-x.md` is inside the ignored path list, so it should produce `code_behind == 0`, and `sync` should report `current` rather than merging. This test instead asserts `out.data["status"] == "merged"` and that `.ddflow/rules/r-x.md` is present. With the documented knob semantics, the test fails for a default-config worktree after landing a rules-only commit; if the implementation instead hard-codes `.ddflow/rules/` as “code” to satisfy the test, then the knob is not authoritative because users cannot suppress rulebook advances even when `behind_ignore_globs` includes `.ddflow/`, contradicting the change’s contract that the configured ignore globs name the paths that do not count.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_code_behind.py:test_sync_still_merges_when_a_rulebook_changed_in_the_ignored_directory (line 163)

The default ignore list keeps .ddflow/ events out; rulebooks stay drift by design. (An earlier triage of this finding with probe 'x' was a mis-typed command; this is the real probe.)

chunk_findings.detail: The test lands only `.ddflow/rules/r-x.md`, which is under the default ignore glob `.ddflow/`, so `code_behind` is `0` under the stated implementation. The ACCEPT rule says sync/queue should skip when code-behind is zero, and the other sync tests enforce that for events-only advances. This test nevertheless asserts `status == "merged"` and that the rule file is present in the worktree. Thus, with the specified default ignore list, the test should fail; if the implementation is changed to make it pass, the ignore knob no longer behaves as a simple path-ignore list and contradicts the intended “skip when K = 0” behavior.

chunk_findings.detail: The new help text says `ddflow sync`, the merge queue, the commit gate’s `max_behind`, and the session-start hint read the code-behind count and “when K is 0 they do nothing (no merge commit)”, then immediately says a rulebook changed under `.ddflow/rules/` “still counts, as `stale_rules`”. With the documented default ignore glob `.ddflow/`, a base advance that only adds `.ddflow/rules/r-x.md` has K=0, so the blanket “do nothing” sentence tells users/agents that sync will not merge it. The added test `test_the_commit_gate_still_blocks_on_a_rulebook_under_the_ignored_directory` asserts the opposite for exactly that input: `sync(...).data["status"] == "merged"` and drift clears. Thus the documentation either omits the required stale-rules exception for sync/commit-gate or contradicts the test’s stated behavior; as written, following the docs leaves the gate’s `stale_rules` block unresolved.

chunk_findings.detail: The change removes the fallback that previously made an unreadable or invalid config behave as “ignore nothing.” If `cfg` is `None` and `Config.load(repo)` raises (for example, a malformed or unreadable local config), `_ignore_globs` now propagates that exception into callers such as the sync/drift path, whereas before it returned `()` and allowed the command to continue with every commit counted. This turns a recoverable configuration problem into a failed command.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/drift.py:_ignore_globs

chunk_findings.detail: The fast path returns “current” only when `rep.rules` is empty. With the default `behind_ignore_globs=[".ddflow/"]`, a missing commit that changes only a rulebook under `.ddflow/` has `code_behind=0` but `rep.rules` non-empty, so branchsync falls through to status `behind` and, when `check=False`, proceeds to merge it. That creates the merge/sync signal the change is meant to remove for `K=0`; the rulebook case should remain drift (`stale_rules`) rather than making the tree “behind” for sync/queue re-merge.

chunk_findings.detail: The new threshold uses `(d.code or 0)` for the comparison but still interpolates `d.code` and `d.behind` directly in the message. The `Drift` dataclass explicitly allows `behind is None` (with `detail` explaining why), and TOML permits a negative integer for `max_behind`. Given `[enforce].max_behind = -1` and a drift result where the base could not be measured (`behind=None`, `code_behind=None`), the condition `(None or 0) > -1` is true, so the verdict is emitted as `... this branch is None commits behind ... None commits in all`. The same negative threshold also flags a branch with `code_behind=0` because `0 > -1`, contradicting the change’s rule that zero code-behind should not make `max_behind` act.
